subject: DPA inquiry — model-improvement exclusion and operational proofs
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@healix.ai>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@healix.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA questions: model-improvement exclusion & evidence pack

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week — Healix's engineering and privacy teams had a few follow-ups as we walk toward an initial pilot. Our legal team wants firm answers on three items before we move to procurement:

1) Absolute confirmation that Healix data will not be used to improve models (no-training / no-derivatives commitment). We need contract language we can include in the DPA and an operational description of how you enforce this.

2) Subprocessor inventory and dataflow diagram showing any offsite processors (KMS, logging, analytics, telemetry). If any processors are outside the US we need residency controls and transfer safeguards.

3) Evidence artifacts: a short proof pack (SOC2 cert or attestation reference, a signed no-train annex draft, and a description of deletion/retention guarantees for prompt/response telemetry).

Attached is a short questionnaire (Questionnaire_HEALIX_v1.xlsx) with formatting that helps our procurement team. Can you confirm what you can provide and a target date for the artifacts? We have an end-of-month target for onboarding so timing matters.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Head of Integrations
HealixAI

[Attachment: Questionnaire_HEALIX_v1.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@healix.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA questions: model-improvement exclusion & evidence pack

Samantha — thanks for the clear list, and great to hear the pilot interest. High-level answers below; Marissa (Legal) and David (Security) are cc'd for details and artifacts.

1) No-training: Redwood can commit to an explicit \"no model training or model improvement\" clause for customer data used via our hosted inference product. We'll provide a draft annex with contract language and the operational controls we use (telemetry minimization, ephemeral KV caching, and an opt-out flag). See attached excerpt from our DPA highlighting the clause.

2) Subprocessors: short answer — we use cloud providers for infra (AWS), a managed logging vendor, and a monitoring analytics provider. We have a subprocessor inventory we can export. David will share the inventory and a dataflow diagram showing where keys and logs live.

3) Evidence pack: we can provide references to our current SOC2 report, the drafted no-train annex, and an operational runbook snippet describing deletion/retention windows for prompt/response telemetry. Marissa will work with you on the precise DPA wording and timing.

Target: we'll circulate the initial pack (DPA excerpt, draft annex, and subprocessor CSV) by April 18. If Healix needs anything sooner for procurement, tell us which items are blockers.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

[Attachment: redwood-dpa-excerpt-no-train.pdf (PDF)]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@healix.ai>, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed DPA Annex language + ops clarifications

Hi Samantha — looping in legal. Per Naomi's note, attached is a short draft Annex that we usually use to memorialize the model-improvement exclusion. Highlights and clarifications:

- Draft Annex A (attached) gives an unequivocal \"Redwood will not use Customer Content to train or improve any model\" statement and an explicit definition of \"Customer Content\" that includes prompts and responses.
- Operationally, we do retain minimal telemetry for debugging (request metadata, non-pii timestamps) for up to 14 days by default, unless you select the dedicated / VPC option which can reduce that to ephemeral-only. We commit to not using any retained telemetry for model training.
- Prompt/response ownership: the annex states Healix retains all rights to prompts and responses. Redwood reserves the right to retain aggregated, de-identified metrics for capacity planning only; we won't derive or ship model improvements from customer content.
- Transfers/subprocessors: we propose a clause that permits onshore-only routing for keys and logs where required; we can also support SFTP export and quarterly attestations.

Can you confirm whether Healix requires a physical onshore KMS (customer-managed) or if a regional (US) cloud KMS is acceptable? Also, which format would procurement prefer for attestation frequency (quarterly written attestation vs. a live SOC2 supplement)?

Thanks — attached: annex-no-train-draft.docx. I can incorporate Healix redlines once we get your team's ask.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head, Legal & Contracts
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

[Attachment: annex-no-train-draft.docx (DOCX)]

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@healix.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA Annex language + ops clarifications

Marissa / Naomi — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups from our legal and security teams (redlines attached):

- Healix wants a stronger deletion guarantee for prompt/response copies. The current 14-day window is too long for our regulated pilot; we propose 48 hours for any retained request/response content unless explicitly consented otherwise.
- We need a subprocessors diagram that shows how data moves from our VPC to Redwood, to KMS, to monitoring. Any external subprocessor outside the US must have EU/UK/US transfer safeguards documented.
- Attestations: procurement prefers written quarterly attestations plus annual SOC2. Quarterly attestation should include a signed statement that no Healix data was used for model improvement in the prior quarter.

Attached our redlines (healix-redlines.docx). Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept 48-hour retention for the hosted pilot and whether the quarterly attestation timeline works? Also please include any evidence that deletion requests are actually executed (S3 object lifecycle, API delete logs, or an export).

Samantha
Head of Integrations, HealixAI

[Attachment: healix-redlines.docx (DOCX)]

From: david.kim@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@healix.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Operational response: retention, subprocessors, and attestations

Samantha — thanks for the redlines and the specificity — below is an operational summary that maps to the DPA language and the annex. Items are actionable and we can include them in the evidence pack we circulate today.

1) Retention: for the hosted pilot we can scope Healix to 48-hour retention for any request/response payloads that would otherwise be logged. That will be enforced via a dedicated tenant flag that triggers immediate lifecycle deletion policies on the telemetry bucket. We will document S3 lifecycle rules and share API delete logs for deletion requests.

2) Subprocessors & dataflow (see attached CSV): current subprocessors by function:
   - Cloud infra: AWS (us-east-1) — compute + S3
   - KMS: AWS KMS (customer may elect a customer-managed KMS in us-east-1)
   - Logging/Monitoring: LogWave Inc. (US-based) — collects only non-pii metrics unless otherwise configured
   - Analytics: MetricsCo (US) — aggregated, de-identified only

We can generate a diagram for your architecture team showing the VPC peering / routing and the key custody flow. All subprocessors listed are within the US; if Healix has an EU residency requirement we'll add regional equivalents and update the transfer safeguards.

3) Attestations: Redwood will provide written quarterly attestations confirming (a) no customer content was used to train models, and (b) deletion requests executed within the agreed SLA. We will also provide our most recent SOC2 report in the evidence pack.

Next steps: we'll upload the following to a secure share by EOD Apr 18: subprocessor_inventory_20280418.csv, the finalized Annex A draft with a 48-hour retention option, SOC2 reference, and the S3 lifecycle snippet showing the 48-hour rule. Let us know if you want the attestation signed by an officer or delivered via portal.

Thanks,
David Kim
Security Engineer, Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai

[Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_20280418.csv (CSV)]
